newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo freight rates end week at new 5-year low.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo freight rates end week at new 5-year low.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) extended a steady decline with a loss of eight more points on Friday to end the week at 1,030.
The BFI has now been in an unbroken slide from 1,119 at the end of August and is recording fresh post-1992 lows on a daily basis. The historic high was 2,532 in May 1995.
The US Gulf/Japan sub-index was again marked lower at 1,354 from 1,362 points on Thursday at a rate of $19.35.
Brokers said Panamaxes remained weak with Handysizes and Capers steadier. The BFI Capesize Route 10 Tubarao/Rotterdam was just down at 987 from Thursday's 989 at $4.988.

Owners were reconciled to further erosion of the BFI and, therefore, of sentiment, noting the weight of Panamax tonnage hanging over the market. "Panamaxes continue to take the beating. There are a lot of Chinese ship and operator tonnage around," said one source.
"Capers are flat. If modern Capesizes do a bit better you may see charterers look to Panamxes and split cargoes".
A flurry of US Gulf/Japan grain fixtures was reported on Friday. Oceanic Enterprise 56,700 tonnes minmax heavy grains was fixed USG/Japan for 20-26 September to Dreyfus at $19.00 without combination.

MSK was reported to have fixed Maricobber 54,000 tonnes heavy grains US Gulf/Japan 18-25 September at $18.50 and Gao Zhou Hai 52,000 tonnes US Gulf/Japan for 13-22 October at $20.25, both with no combination.
Sanki was reported to have taken Japanese tonnage for 54,000 tonnes US Gulf/Japan for 1-15 October at $19.00, again without combination, but details were sought.

In coal trades 1971-built Delta Peace 60,000 dwt secured $5.25 fixed to Seatrans Richards Bay/Lisbon for 15-30 September. Far East timecharters for modern tonnage included 1994-built Samarinda 149,647 dwt to Samsun delivery South Japan end September trip via Saldanha redelivery South Korea at $9,400 daily.
Volume was thin by mid-afternoon on BIFFEX futures with September most-traded, in 57 lots, down 10 at 1,020 and October lower by 15 at 1,120. Brokers pegged support at 1,098 basis October.
Ship completions were running ahead of new orders during the first half of 1996 according to the latest issue of World Shipbuilding Statistics published by Lloyds Register.
At end June this year the world order book stood at 45 million gross tonnage, down 3.5 million since end-December 1995.
